take_rate.definition: Revenue divided by Total Payment Volume; measures percentage of transaction volume converted to revenue

tpv.definition: Total Payment Volume; aggregate value of all transactions processed through the platform

interchange.definition: Fee paid by the acquiring bank to the issuing bank for each card transaction

authorization_rate.definition: Percentage of payment requests successfully approved by the card issuer/network

chargeback_rate.definition: Ratio of disputed transactions reversed by card network to total transactions
chargeback_rate.threshold: Card networks may impose penalties above 1%

settlement_accuracy.definition: Percentage of settlements correctly reconciled without discrepancy

tokenization.definition: Process of replacing sensitive cardholder data (PANs) with non-sensitive equivalents (tokens), reducing PCI-DSS scope

3ds.definition: 3-D Secure; authentication protocol required by card networks for e-commerce transactions to reduce fraud

bsa_aml.name: Bank Secrecy Act / Anti-Money Laundering
bsa_aml.sar_filing: 30 days from detection of suspicious activity

pci_dss.name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard

product_to_compliance.trigger: New product or feature requiring compliance review

rag_chunks: Take Rate is Revenue divided by Total Payment Volume (TPV). It measures the percentage of transaction volume converted to revenue and is a primary KPI for payments fintechs tracked by CFOs and CEOs.

Interchange is the fee paid by the acquiring bank to the issuing bank for each card transaction. Scheme fees are charged by card networks (Visa, Mastercard). Authorization rate measures the percentage of payment requests approved — benchmark is >95%. Chargeback rate is disputed transactions as a percentage of volume — threshold is <0.5%.

3-D Secure (3DS) is an authentication protocol required by card networks for online transactions. Tokenization replaces sensitive cardholder data with non-sensitive equivalents, reducing PCI-DSS scope. Both are key compliance technologies for payment processors.

BSA/AML compliance requires: Currency Transaction Reports (CTR) for transactions exceeding $10,000 in aggregate per day. Suspicious Activity Reports (SAR) must be filed within 30 days of detection. Red flags include structuring (breaking transactions to avoid thresholds), rapid movement of funds, and unusual transaction patterns. KYC components include CIP, CDD, and EDD.

PCI-DSS compliance levels: Level 1 (>6M transactions/year), Level 2 (1-6M), Level 3 (20K-1M e-commerce), Level 4 (<20K e-commerce). Requirements include cardholder data protection, encryption, access controls, and network security.

Head of Payments KPIs: authorization rate >95%, settlement accuracy 99.99%, uptime availability 99.99%, dispute rate <0.5%. Payment routing decisions consider cost, success rate, speed, customer experience, and risk profile.

BSA Officer role: Financial Crime Prevention Expert. Evaluates suspicious activity based on transaction_patterns, customer_profile, red_flags_identified, documentation_available. Outputs: investigation_result, sar_recommendation, account_action. Escalates to CCO.

Fintech compliance handoffs: Product→Compliance (new product review, SLA: 2 business day response, 5 day completion). BSA→Compliance (suspicious activity, SAR filing within 30 days). Required context includes PRD, data handling, customer segments, and state licensing plan.
